Real exam mechanics actively researched but could NOT be confirmed: checked the full manual text (no mention anywhere of a specific item count, passing score/percentage, or time limit for the written knowledge test), WYDOT's official Testing Requirements page (dot.state.wy.us/home/driver_license_records/driver-license/testing.html -- describes the written test only as covering 'questions related to the class of license you are applying for' plus seat belt/other laws, with no published item count or passing score), WYDOT's official Frequently Asked Questions page (no mechanics listed), and the governing statute W.S. 31-7-114 'Examinations; visual acuity' (fetched via wyoleg.gov's official Title 31 statutes compilation -- confirms the division must test knowledge of traffic control devices, safe driving practices and traffic laws, but specifies no question count, passing score, or time limit). The manual and testing page do confirm applicants may take the written test twice in one day, and that a driving-skills-test retest is delayed to three days if the applicant 'misses 13 or more questions' on the SKILLS test scoring sheet (a distinct, unrelated scored checklist for the road test, not the written knowledge exam) -- this skills-test detail is reflected in the question bank but is explicitly NOT conflated with the unconfirmed written-test item count/passing score. Per instructions, these mechanics are reported as genuinely UNCONFIRMED rather than guessed or defaulted to another state's numbers. Content-depth rationale: this is a substantial, fact-dense manual (98 pages / ~4,755 lines) with many concrete, quotable, testable figures throughout -- exact GDL age/hour thresholds (50 hours incl. 10 night hours; 16.5 with 6-month intermediate license), speed limit table, BAC thresholds (0.08 adult / 0.02 youthful / 0.05 supporting-evidence), detailed DWUI suspension/revocation/ignition-interlock schedules by offense number, child restraint fines ($60/$110) and FMVSS 213 requirement, following-distance multipliers by condition (2/4/6/8 seconds), parking/fire-hydrant distances, headlight dimming distances (500 ft/300 ft), Move Over Law specifics (20 mph reduction), sign-shape meanings, railroad-crossing procedures, and a full definitions glossary. This comfortably supports a rich, non-repetitive, fully-grounded bank: 282 questions were written across 27 topic buckets (licensing classes & GDL, testing & documentation, fees & renewals, intermediate & restricted GDL licenses, vehicle equipment, safety belts & child restraints, traffic sign shapes/colors, signals & pavement markings, railroad crossings, speed limits & adjusting speed, right-of-way/intersections/roundabouts, required stops & school buses, changing lanes & turning, passing rules, parking rules, interstate driving, traffic crashes, sharing the road with motorcycles/bicycles/heavy vehicles, sharing the road with animals/pedestrians, defensive driving & space cushion, reduced light & night driving, weather conditions, emergency situations, DUI/alcohol/drug law, suspensions/revocations/penalties, health/vision/hearing/distracted driving, and definitions/misc services), each grounded in and cited to specific quoted manual (or, for exam-mechanics/statute questions, official WYDOT/statute) text via source_note, with no invented facts. This is a brand-new Wyoming Driver track -- Wyoming's existing site content is limited to an unrelated notary track; no prior WY driver content exists on the site, and no WY notary files were modified in this work.
